<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Allowance for Loan Losses</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance for loan losses is a valuation allowance available for losses incurred on loans.&#160;&#160;All losses are charged to the allowance for loan losses when the loss actually occurs or when a determination is made that a loss is likely to occur.&#160;&#160;Recoveries are credited to the allowance at the time of recovery.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance is an amount that represents the amount of probable and reasonably estimable known and inherent losses in the loan portfolio, based on evaluations of the collectability of loans.&#160;&#160;The evaluations take into consideration such factors as changes in the types and amount of loans in the loan portfolio, historical loss experience, adverse situations that may affect the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay, estimated value of any underlying collateral, estimated losses relating to specifically identified loans, and current economic conditions.&#160;&#160;This evaluation is inherently subjective as it requires material estimates including, among others, exposure at default, the amount and timing of expected future cash flows on impacted loans, value of collateral, estimated losses on our commercial and residential loan portfolios and general amounts for historical loss experience.&#160;&#160;All of these estimates may be susceptible to significant change.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">It should be understood that estimates of future loan losses involve an exercise of judgment.&#160;&#160;While it is possible that in particular periods the Company may sustain losses, which are substantial relative to the allowance for loan losses, it is the judgment of management that the allowance for loan losses reflected in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets is adequate to absorb possible losses in the existing loan portfolio.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loans Held-for-Sale</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans held-for-sale include originated mortgage loans intended for sale in the secondary market, which are carried at the lower of cost or estimated market value.&#160;&#160;Loans held-for-sale are identified at the time of origination, in accordance with the Company&#8217;s interest rate risk strategy.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company occasionally sells loans that it originates, but cannot hold, due to regulatory limitations on loans to one borrower, concentrations of credit in a particular property type or industry.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loan Fees, Loan Costs, Discounts and Premiums</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loan origination and commitment fees and certain direct loan origination costs are deferred and amortized as an adjustment to the related loan&#8217;s yield using the interest method over the contractual life of the loan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Discounts received in connection with mortgage loans purchased are amortized to income over the term of the loan using the interest method.&#160;&#160;Premiums on purchased loans are amortized over the term of the loan using the interest method.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Real Estate Owned</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Real estate acquired through, or in lieu of, loan foreclosure is initially recorded at fair value, less estimated cost to sell, at the date of foreclosure and any related write-down is charged to the allowance for loan losses.&#160;&#160;Management periodically performs valuations, and an allowance for losses will be established when any significant and permanent decline reduces the fair value to less than the carrying value.&#160;&#160;The ability of the Company to recover the carrying value of real estate is based upon future sales of the real estate owned.&#160;&#160;The ability to affect such sales is subject to market conditions and other factors, many of which are beyond the Company&#8217;s control.&#160;&#160;Operating income of such properties, net of related expenses, and gains and losses on their disposition are included in the accompanying consolidated statements of income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are reflected at currently enacted income tax rates applicable to the period in which the deferred tax assets and liabilities are expected to be realized or settled.&#160;&#160;As changes in tax laws or rates are enacted, deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted through the provision for income taxes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">When tax returns are filed, it is highly certain that some positions taken would be sustained upon examination by the taxing authorities, while others are subject to uncertainty about the merits of the position taken or the amount of the position that would be ultimately sustained.&#160;&#160;The benefit of a tax position is recognized in the financial statements in the period during which, based on all available evidence, management believes it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination, including the resolution of appeals or litigation processes, if any.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Tax positions taken are not offset or aggregated with other positions.&#160;&#160;Tax positions that meet the more-likely-than-not recognition threshold are measured as the largest amount of tax benefit that is more than 50% likely of being realized upon settlement with the applicable taxing authority.&#160;&#160;The portion of the benefits associated with tax positions taken that exceeds the amount measured as described above would be reflected as a liability for unrecognized tax benefits in the consolidated balance sheets along with any associated interest or penalties that would be </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">payable to the taxing authorities upon examination.&#160;&#160;Interest and/or penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits, if any, would be classified as additional income taxes in the consolidated statements of income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Advertising Costs</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company expenses advertising costs as incurred.&#160; Advertising costs were $366,000, $256,000 and $158,000 for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Comprehensive Earnings</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accounting principles generally require that recognized revenue, expenses, gains and losses be included in net income.&#160;&#160;Although certain changes in assets and liabilities, such as unrealized gains and losses on available-for-sale securities, are reported as a separate component of the equity section of the consolidated balance sheets, such items, along with net earnings, are components of comprehensive earnings.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Use of Estimates</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In preparing financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, management is required to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities as of the date of the consolidated balance sheets and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from those estimates.&#160;&#160;Material estimates that are particularly susceptible to significant change relate to the determination of the allowance for losses on loans and deferred taxes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2013, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) 2013-10, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Inclusion of the Fed Funds Effective Swap Rate as a Benchmark Interest Rate for Hedge Accounting Purposes</font>, in order to permit the Fed Funds Effective Swap Rate to be used as a U.S. benchmark interest rate for hedge accounting purposes under ASC Topic 815, in addition to the U.S. Treasury rates and the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).&#160;&#160;ASU 2013-10 also removes the restriction on using different benchmark rates for similar hedges.&#160;&#160;The amendments were effective for qualifying new or redesignated hedging relationships entered into on or after July 17, 2013.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this guidance had no impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2013, the FASB issued ASU 2013-11, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Presentation of an Unrecognized Tax Benefit When a Net Operating Loss Carryforward, a Similar Tax Loss, or a Tax Credit Carryfowrard Exists</font>.&#160;&#160;This guidance requires an unrecognized tax benefit, or a portion of an unrecognized tax benefit, be presented in the financial statements as a reduction to a deferred tax asset for a net operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss, or a tax credit carryforward.&#160;&#160;If a net operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss, or a tax credit carryforward is not available at the reporting date, the unrecognized tax benefit should be presented in the financial statements as a liability and not combined with deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;This guidance is effective for public entities for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2013.&#160;&#160;For nonpublic entities, the amendments are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2014.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this guidance is not expected to have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Recent Accounting Pronouncements (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In January 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-01, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Investments-Equity Method and Joint Ventures - Accounting for Investments in Qualified Affordable Housing Projects.&#160;&#160;</font>This guidance permits reporting entities to make an accounting policy election to account for their investments in qualified affordable housing projects using the proportional amortization method if certain conditions are met.&#160;&#160;Under the proportional amortization method, an entity amortizes the initial cost of the investment in proportion to the tax credits and other tax benefits received and recognizes the net investment performance in the income statement as a component of income tax expense (benefit).&#160;&#160;For those investments in qualified affordable housing projects not accounted for using the proportional amortization method, the investment should be accounted for as an equity method investment or a cost method investment.&#160;&#160;This guidance is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2014.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this guidance is not expected to have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In January 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-04, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Reclassification of Residential Real Estate - Collateralized Consumer Mortgage Loans upon Foreclosure</font>.&#160;&#160;The guidance within ASU 2014-04 clarifies that an in-substance repossession or foreclosure occurs, and a creditor is considered to have received physical possession of residential real estate property collateralizing a consumer mortgage loan, upon either (a) the creditor obtaining legal title to the residential real estate property upon completion of a foreclosure, or (b) the borrower conveying all interest in the residential real estate property to the creditor to satisfy the loan through completion of a deed in lieu of foreclosure or through a similar legal agreement.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the amendments require interim and annual disclosure of both (a) the amount of foreclosed residential real estate property held by the creditor and (b) the recorded investment in consumer mortgage loans collateralized by residential real estate property that are in the process of foreclosure according to local requirements of the applicable jurisdiction.&#160;&#160;ASU 2014-04 is effective for public business entities for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2014.&#160;&#160;For entities other than public business entities, the amendments of ASU 2014-04 are effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2014.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this of this guidance is not expected to have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September 2013, the Internal Revenue Service released the final tangible property regulations for Sections 162(a) and 263(a) of the Internal Revenue Code, regarding the deduction and capitalization of amounts paid to acquire, produce, or improve tangible property.&#160;&#160;The final regulations replace temporary regulations that were issued in December 2011 and are effective for tax years beginning January 1, 2014.&#160;&#160;The application of the final regulations is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank uses the following criteria to assess risk ratings with respect to its loan portfolio, which are consistent with regulatory guidelines:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 54pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Special Mention - </font>Loans designated as &#8220;special mention&#8221; exhibit some weakness or risk that deserves management&#8217;s close attention, but do not contain the level of risk associated with an adverse classification.&#160;&#160;If left unresolved, this weakness may develop into a material deficiency in the credit quality of the loan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 54pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Substandard - </font>Loans classified as &#8220;substandard&#8221; have a well-defined material weakness or weaknesses based on objective evidence and are further characterized by the distinct possibility that the Bank will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are not corrected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 54pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loss - </font>Loans classified as &#8220;loss&#8221; are considered uncollectible, in whole or in part, and should not be carried on the books as an asset without the establishment of a specific valuation allowance or charge-off.&#160;&#160;This classification does not mean that an asset has no salvage value, but there is much doubt about how much, or when, the recovery will occur.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 3.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Loans (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following table summarizes the credit grades assigned to our loan portfolio as of December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Federal Home Loan Bank Advances</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to collateral agreements with the Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;), advances issued by the Federal Home Loan Bank are secured by a blanket floating lien on first mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;Total interest expense recognized on FHLB advances in 2013, 2012 and 2011, was $1,087,000, $1,160,000, and $1,470,000, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 10.&#160;&#160;Regulatory Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by its primary federal regulator, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (&#8220;OCC&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Failure to meet the minimum regulatory capital requirements can result in certain mandatory, and possible additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the Bank and the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;Under the regulatory capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines involving quantitative measures of the Bank&#8217;s assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s capital amounts and classification under the prompt corrective action guidelines are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings, and other factors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios of:&#160;&#160;total risk-based capital and Tier I capital to risk-weighted assets (as defined in the regulations), Tier I capital to adjusted total assets (as defined), tangible capital to adjusted total assets (as defined), and tangible equity to adjusted total assets (as defined).&#160;&#160;As of December&#160;31,&#160;2013, the Bank met all of the capital requirements to which it is subject and was deemed to be well capitalized.&#160;&#160;There have been no subsequent conditions or events which management believes have changed the Bank&#8217;s status.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 11.&#160;&#160;Financial Instruments with Off-Balance Sheet Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has entered into certain credit related commitments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business in order to meet the financing needs of its customers.&#160;&#160;The financial instruments include commitments to extend credit and commitments to sell loans.&#160;&#160;Such commitments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk in excess of the amount recognized in the financial statements.&#160;&#160;The contract amounts of those instruments reflect the extent of the involvement the Company has in particular classes of financial instruments.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s exposure to credit loss is represented by the contractual amount of these commitments.&#160;&#160;The Company follows the same credit policies in making commitments as it does for on-balance sheet instruments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">no violation of any condition established in the commitment.&#160;&#160;Commitments generally have </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require payment of a fee.&#160;&#160;The commitments for lines of credit may expire without being drawn upon.&#160;&#160;Therefore, the total commitment amounts do not necessarily represent future cash requirements.&#160;&#160;The amount of collateral obtained, if it is deemed necessary by the Company, is based on management&#8217;s credit evaluation of the customer.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013 and 2012, the Company had outstanding commitments to extend credit totaling approximately $33,330,000 and $31,768,000, respectively, and had no commitments to sell loans at a loss.&#160; Of the $33,330,000 in outstanding commitments at December&#160;31,&#160;2013, approximately $6,991,000 were for fixed rate loans with interest rates ranging from 3.25% to 5.88%, and approximately $26,339,000 were for variable rate loans with interest ranging from 3.25% to 9.50%.&#160;&#160;No material losses or gains are anticipated as a result of these outstanding commitments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 13.&#160;&#160;Concentration of Credit Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In accordance with industry practices, the Company has deposits in other financial institutions for more than the federally insured limit.&#160;&#160;These deposits in other institutions do not represent more than the normal industry credit risk.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 14.&#160;&#160;Estimated Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following disclosure is made in accordance with the requirements of ASC 825, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Financial Instruments</font>.&#160;&#160;Financial instruments are defined as cash and contractual rights and obligations that require settlement, directly or indirectly, in cash.&#160;&#160;In cases where quoted market prices are not available, fair values have been estimated using the present value of future cash flows or other valuation techniques.&#160;&#160;The results of these techniques are highly sensitive to the assumptions </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">used, such as those concerning appropriate discount rates and estimates of future cash flows, </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">which require considerable judgment.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, estimates presented herein are not necessarily indicative of the amounts the Company could realize in a current settlement of the underlying financial instruments.&#160;&#160;ASC 825 excludes certain financial instruments and all nonfinancial instruments from its disclosure requirements.&#160;&#160;These disclosures should not be interpreted as representing an aggregate measure of the underlying value of the Company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following methods and assumptions were used by the Company in estimating fair value disclosures for financial instruments:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The carrying amount of cash and due from financial institutions, federal funds sold and short-term investments approximates fair value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Certificates of Deposit</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair values for certificates of deposit are estimated through discounted cash flow analysis, using current rates at which certificates of deposit with similar terms could be obtained.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">93</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="4">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 14.&#160;&#160;Estimated Fair Value of Financial Instruments (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Securities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair values for securities, excluding Federal Home Loan Bank stock, are based on quoted market prices.&#160;&#160;If quoted market prices are not available, fair values are based on quoted market prices of comparable instruments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loans Receivable, Net</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair values of loans are estimated through discounted cash flow analysis, using current rates at which loans with similar terms would be made to borrowers with similar credit quality.&#160;&#160;Appropriate adjustments are made to reflect probable credit losses.&#160;&#160;The carrying amount of accrued interest on loans approximated its fair value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Federal Home Loan Bank Stock</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The carrying value of Federal Home Loan Bank stock approximates fair value based on the redemption provisions of the Federal Home Loan Bank.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Deposit Liabilities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ASC 825 specifies that the fair value of deposit liabilities with no defined maturity is the amount payable on demand at the reporting date, i.e., their carrying or book value.&#160;&#160;These deposits include interest and non-interest bearing checking, passbook, and money market accounts.&#160;&#160;The fair value </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">of fixed rate certificates of deposit is estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">applies interest rates currently offered on certificates of similar remaining maturities to a schedule of aggregate expected cash flows on time deposits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Borrowings</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair value of fixed rate borrowings is estimated using discounted cash flows, based on current incremental borrowing rates for similar types of borrowing arrangements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Off-Balance Sheet Instruments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Off-balance sheet financial instruments include commitments to extend credit and undisbursed lines of credit.&#160;&#160;The fair value of such instruments is estimated using fees currently charged for similar arrangements in the marketplace, adjusted for changes in terms and credit risk as appropriate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company adopted ASC 820, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Fair Value Measurements</font>, on January 1, 2008 for all financial assets and liabilities and nonfinancial assets and liabilities that are recognized at fair value in the financial statements on a recurring basis (at least annually).&#160;&#160;ASC 820 defines fair value, establishes a framework for measuring fair value, and expands disclosures about fair value measurements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ASC 820 defines fair value as the price that would be received upon sale of an asset or paid upon transfer of a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date and in the principal or most advantageous market for that asset or liability.&#160;&#160;The fair value should be calculated based on assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability, not on assumptions specific to the entity.&#160;&#160;In addition, the fair value of liabilities should include consideration of non-performance risk including the Company&#8217;s own credit risk.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<hr style="COLOR: black" align="left" noshade size="1" width="100%">
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 14.&#160;&#160;Estimated Fair Value of Financial Instruments (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to defining fair value, ASC 820 expands the disclosure requirements around fair value and establishes a fair value hierarchy for valuation inputs.&#160;&#160;The hierarchy prioritizes the inputs into three levels based on the extent to which inputs used in measuring fair value are observable in the market.&#160;&#160;Each fair value measurement is reported in one of the three levels which is determined by the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety.&#160;&#160;These levels are:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font></div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 1 - Inputs are based upon unadjusted quoted prices for identical instruments traded in active markets.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font></div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 2 - Inputs are based upon quoted prices for similar instruments in active markets, quoted prices for identical or similar instruments in markets that are not active, and model-based valuation techniques for which all significant assumptions are observable in the market or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font></div>
</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 3 - Inputs are generally unobservable and typically reflect management&#8217;s estimates of assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.&#160;&#160;The fair values are therefore determined using model-based techniques that include option pricing models, discounted cash flow models, and similar techniques.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The preceding methods described may produce a fair value calculation that may not be indicative of the net realizable value or reflective of future fair values.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, although the Company believes its valuation methods are appropriate and consistent with other market participants, the use of different methodologies or assumptions to determine the fair value of certain financial instruments could result in a different fair value measurement at the reporting date.&#160;&#160;There have been no changes in the methodologies used during the year ended December 31, 2013.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">LOUISIANA BANCORP, INC.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements </font></font>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 15.&#160;&#160;Employee Benefits</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank has a 401(k) plan covering all employees who meet certain age and service requirements.&#160;&#160;Contributions to the plan are made at the discretion of the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;The 401(k) </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">expense amounted to approximately $22,000, $18,000 and $13,000 for the years ended December&#160;31,&#160;2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.&#160;&#160;The plan contains profit sharing provisions, </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">with employer contributions to the plan based on a percentage of wages, net of forfeitures.&#160;&#160;There was no profit sharing contribution during 2013, 2012 or 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank adopted a Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan (&#8220;SERP&#8221;) during 2006 for its Chief Executive Officer.&#160;&#160;The agreement requires the Bank&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer to remain employed by the Bank through January 15, 2013 in exchange for retirement benefits payable in equal quarterly installments of $25,000 for ten consecutive years.&#160;&#160;In the event of disability, the Bank&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer is entitled to receive equal quarterly installments of $25,000 for ten consecutive years.&#160;&#160;In the event of termination, other than for disability, the Bank&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer is entitled to benefits accrued through that period.&#160;&#160;In the event of death, benefits will </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">be payable to the Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s designated beneficiary.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;31,&#160;2013, 2012 and 2011, the Bank accrued $91,000, $100,000 and $95,000, respectively, in accordance with this agreement.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s future compensation expense for 2014 under this plan is $38,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective January 15, 2013, the Board of Directors adopted an amendment to the SERP agreement for its Chief Executive Officer which was intended to serve as an inducement to continue his service beyond the age of 65.&#160;&#160;This amendment increases the annual benefit payable to the Bank&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer by $5,000 per annum, beginning January 15, 2014 and ending January 15, 2018.&#160;&#160;The maximum annual benefit payable to the Chief Executive Officer as a result of this amendment is $125,000, paid in quarterly installments.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s estimated future compensation expense as a result of this amendment is $50,000 per year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In March 2007, the Bank implemented a SERP for the benefit of the Bank&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer.&#160;&#160;The Plan provides for annual credits to an accumulation account at the rate of 10% of </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">the Executive&#8217;s annual base pay.&#160;&#160;The account is credited with earnings on an annual basis at a </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">rate determined by the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;The Executive will be fully vested (100%) in his Accumulation Account at age 65.&#160;&#160;The Plan provides for partial vesting when the Executive reaches the &#8220;Early Retirement Age&#8221; of 55 and remains in the employ of the Bank.&#160;&#160;Upon reaching the Early Retirement Age, the Executive will be vested 75% in the Accumulation Account.&#160;&#160;Additional vesting will be credited at the rate of 2.5% per annum for years of service after attaining the </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Early Retirement Age.&#160;&#160;Notwithstanding the other provisions of the agreement, the Executive </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">will be 100% vested in the Accumulation Account in the event of death, permanent disability, termination without cause, or termination following a change of control.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;31,<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>2013, 2012 and 2011, the Bank accrued $12,700, $12,000 and $11,600, respectively, in accordance with this agreement in the respective periods.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 16.&#160;&#160;Related Party Transactions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank purchased insurance policies through an insurance agency of which one of its directors is an executive officer.&#160;&#160;Premiums for such policies totaled $597,000, $517,000 and $427,000 for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements </font></font></font>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 17.&#160;&#160;Employee Stock Ownership Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2007, Louisiana Bancorp, Inc. instituted an employee stock ownership plan.&#160;&#160;The Louisiana Bancorp Employee Stock Ownership Plan (&#8220;ESOP&#8221;) enables all eligible employees of the Bank to share in the growth of the Company through the acquisition of stock.&#160;&#160;Employees are generally eligible to participate in the ESOP after completion of one year of service and attaining age 21.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The ESOP purchased eight percent of the shares offered in the initial public offering of the Company (507,659 shares).&#160;&#160;This purchase was facilitated by a loan from the Company to the ESOP in the amount of $5,077,000.&#160;&#160;The loan is secured by a pledge of the ESOP shares.&#160;&#160;The shares pledged as collateral are reported as unearned ESOP shares in the consolidated balance sheets.&#160;&#160;The corresponding note is being paid back in 80 equal quarterly payments of $130,000 on the last business day of each quarter, beginning September 30, 2007, at the rate of 8.25%.&#160;&#160;The note payable and the corresponding note receivable have been eliminated for consolidation purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company may contribute to the plan, in the form of debt service, at the discretion of its Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;Dividends received on the ESOP shares are utilized to service the debt.&#160;&#160;Shares are released for allocation to plan participants based on principal and interest payments of the note.&#160;&#160;Compensation expense is recognized based on the number of shares allocated to plan participants each year and the average market price of the stock for the current year.&#160;&#160;Released ESOP shares become outstanding for earnings per share computations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As compensation expense is incurred, the unearned ESOP shares account is reduced based on the original cost of the stock.&#160;&#160;The difference between the cost and average market price of shares released for allocation is applied to additional paid-in capital.&#160;&#160;ESOP compensation expense was approximately $441,000, $410,000, and $392,000 for the years ended December&#160;31,&#160;2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 18.&#160;&#160;Recognition and Retention Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 14, 2008, the shareholders of Louisiana Bancorp approved the Company&#8217;s </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2007 Recognition and Retention Plan.&#160;&#160;The 2007 Recognition and Retention Plan provides the Company&#8217;s directors and key employees with an equity interest in the Company as compensation for their contributions to the success of the Company, and as an incentive for future such contributions.&#160;&#160;The Compensation Committee of the Company makes grants under the 2007 Recognition and Retention Plan to eligible participants based on these factors.&#160;&#160;Plan participants vest in their share awards at a rate of 20% per year over a five year period, beginning on the date of the plan share award.&#160;&#160;If service to the Company is terminated for any reason other than death, disability or change in control, the unvested shares awards shall be forfeited.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Recognition and Retention Plan Trust (the &#8220;Trust&#8221;) has been established to acquire, hold, administer, invest, and make distributions from the Trust in accordance with provisions of the Plan and Trust.&#160;&#160;The Trust acquired 4%, or 253,829 shares, of the then issued and outstanding shares of the Company, which are held pursuant to the plan&#8217;s vesting requirements.&#160;&#160;The Recognition and Retention Plan provides that grants to each officer or employee and non-employee director shall not exceed 25% and 5%, respectively.&#160;&#160;Shares awarded to non-employee directors in the aggregate shall not exceed 30% of the shares available under the plan.&#160;&#160;As of December&#160;31,&#160;2013, 243,677 shares had been awarded under the provisions of the plan to directors, officers and employees of the Company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company recognized compensation expense during 2013 at a weighted-average per-share grant date fair value of $12.96.&#160;&#160;Compensation expense related to the Recognition and Retention Plan was $117,000, $526,000 and $521,000 for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2013, there were 16,902 shares available for future grants under the plan, which includes 6,750 shares that were forfeited by former participants in the plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note 19.&#160; </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stock Option Plan</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 14, 2008, the shareholders of Louisiana Bancorp, Inc. also approved the Company&#8217;s 2007 Stock Option Plan.&#160;&#160;The 2007 Stock Option Plan provides the Company&#8217;s directors and key employees with an equity interest in the Company as compensation for their contributions to the success of the Company, and as an incentive for future such contributions.&#160;&#160;The Compensation Committee of the Company grants options to eligible participants based on these factors.&#160;&#160;Plan participants vest in their options at a rate of 20% per year over a five year period, beginning on the grant date of the option.&#160;&#160;Vested options have an exercise period of ten years commencing on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;If service to the Company is terminated for any reason other than death, disability or change in control, the unvested options shall be forfeited.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the terms of the Stock Option Plan, 634,573 shares, or 10%, of common stock of the Company at the time of the plan&#8217;s adoption have been reserved for future issuance.&#160;&#160;The Stock Option Plan provides that grants to each officer or employee and non-employee director shall not exceed 25% and 5%, respectively.&#160;&#160;Options granted to non-employee directors in the aggregate shall not exceed 30% of the shares available under the plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, options to acquire 596,697 shares of common stock had been granted under the provisions of the plan to directors, officers and employees of the Company, at a weighted-average exercise price of $12.03.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2013, there were 70,876 stock options available for future grants under the plan, which includes 33,000 options that were forfeited by former participants in the plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company recognizes compensation expense during the vesting period based on the fair value of the option on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The Company awarded 8,500 options to directors, officers, or employees during the year ended December 31, 2013 having an estimated fair value on their grant date of $2.75, as determined by use of the Black-Scholes Option Pricing Model with the following assumptions:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our management evaluated, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934) as of December 31, 2013.&#160;&#160;Based on such evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we file or submit under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and regulations and are operating in an effective manner.</font></div>
